title: The four in Sunni reckoning
hookLine: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali: the Rightly Guided Caliphs for Sunni Muslims

cards: Four names, in order. Abu Bakr. Umar.
Uthman. Ali. Each has had his own days on this path: a first speech, a register, a single reading of the Qur'an, a shield brought before a judge.
In Sunni Islam, those four names are also said together, in that order, as one group with one title. In a Friday sermon, the preacher may name all four and ask God to be pleased with them.
Today: the four in Sunni reckoning.

teach.h: KHULAFA': THE ONES WHO COME AFTER.
teach.b: The title is al-khulafa' al-rashidun: the rightly guided caliphs. Khulafa' is the plural of khalifah, successor, the one who comes after. Rashidun means rightly guided, people who walk on the straight road.
The phrase leans on a hadith.

teach.h: HOLD TO MY WAY AND THEIRS.
teach.b: In it, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gives his companions a farewell counsel: hold to my way, and the way of the rightly guided successors after me, and grip it tightly. Sunni scholars read those successors as these four.
Each of the four came to office by a different route.
The Sunni telling looks at those four doors and sees one community walking through all of them, so the four belong together, in that order.
Their time is held up as the model of what rule under God should look like, even with its wars and its grief. Here is the detail worth keeping. Ali stands fourth in this Sunni list.
In Shia Islam, Ali stands first, as the first Imam. The same man, honored in both, counted from a different place.
Sunni Muslims love Ali as the fourth of the four and as the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law. Shia Muslims love him as the one the Prophet named. Neither side leaves him out.

how: Sunni Muslims name Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali together as the Rightly Guided Caliphs, often adding 'may God be pleased with him' after each name, and some Friday sermons mention all four.

games.q: you're putting the four in the Sunni order. who comes fourth?
games.why: Ali is fourth in the Sunni list, and first among the Imams for Shia Muslims: the same man, counted from a different place.

practice: Say the four names quietly, in order, one per breath: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, and with each, recall one thing from his days on this path: a speech, a register, a page, a shield.
In Sunni practice each name is followed by: may God be pleased with him. If you pray, you can add it too.

wordCard.voice: Al-khulafa' al-rashidun. The rightly guided caliphs: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, named together, in order, in Sunni Islam. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the rightly guided successors, the Sunni title for the first four caliphs.

carryVoice: Your line: the four. Fourth here, first there, and loved in both. Day eight hundred ninety-eight, done.
